field_summary:
WASHINGTON, March 28, 2025 – Cargill Kitchen Solutions, a company in Lake Odessa, Michigan, is recalling approximately 212,268 pounds of liquid egg products that may contain a cleaning solution with sodium hypochlorite, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced today.

The liquid egg products were produced on March 12 and 13, 2025. The following products are subject to recall: [See the Labels]:

  • Box of 32 oz. (2 lb.) containing “egg beaters ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE” (Original Liquid Egg Substitute) with a "USE BY" date of August 10, 2025.
  • Box of 32 oz. (2 lb.) containing “egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE” (Cage-Free Original Liquid Egg Substitute) with a "USE BY" date of August 9, 2025.
  • Box of 32 oz. (2 lb.) containing “egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL FROZEN EGG SUBSTITUTE” (Cage-Free Frozen Original Liquid Egg Substitute) with a "USE BY" date of August 7, 2026.
  • Box of 32 oz. (2 lb.) containing “Bob Evans Better’n Eggs Made with Real Egg Whites” (Better'n Eggs made with real egg whites Bob Evans) with a "USE BY" date of August 10, 2025.

The recalled product is marked with the establishment number "G'1804" printed in ink on the box. These products were shipped to distributors in Ohio and Texas for use by food service establishments in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, and Iowa. There is a possibility that these products may have been distributed nationwide.

The problem was discovered when FSIS received information about potential contamination of these products. After conducting an investigation and thorough evaluation of the cleaning solution contents, FSIS scientists concluded that using this product should not cause adverse health effects or the risk is insignificant, hence a Class III recall is being conducted.

While FSIS does not expect adverse health effects from consuming products in a Class III recall and there have been no confirmed reports of illnesses due to consumption of these products, anyone with concerns about illness should contact their healthcare provider.

FSIS is concerned because part of the product may be in consumers' refrigerators or freezers. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and food service establishments are advised not to serve them. These products should be discarded or returned to the place of purchase.

FSIS routinely conducts effectiveness checks to verify that companies that have initiated a recall notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to ensure that the product is no longer available to consumers.

Consumers with questions about this recall can contact Chuck Miller, Cargill Kitchen Solutions, at 1-844-419-1574 or media@cargill.com.

Consumers with questions regarding food safety may call the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 1-888-MPHotline (1-888-674-6854) or send a question via email to MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers wishing to report a problem with meat, poultry, or egg products can submit their concerns through the online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
